content: 1. Aspirin, citric acid, and sodium bicarbonate can increase the levels or effects of intranasal ketorolac by competing with acidic (anionic) drugs for renal tubular clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 2. Aspirin, citric acid, and sodium bicarbonate reduce the levels of L-methylfolate by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown. 3. Aspirin, citric acid, and sodium bicarbonate can increase the levels or effects of lornoxicam through acidic (anionic) drug competition for renal tubular clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 4. Aspirin, citric acid, and sodium bicarbonate can increase the levels or effects of meclofenamate by competing with acidic (anionic) drugs for renal tubular clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 5. Aspirin, citric acid, and sodium bicarbonate can increase the levels or effects of mefenamic acid via acidic (anionic) drug competition for renal tubular clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 6. Aspirin, citric acid, and sodium bicarbonate can increase the levels or effects of meloxicam by competing with acidic (anionic) drugs for renal tubular clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 7. Aspirin, citric acid, and sodium bicarbonate can increase the levels or effects of mesalamine through acidic (anionic) drug competition for renal tubular clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 8. Methyclothiazide can increase the levels or effects of aspirin, citric acid, and sodium bicarbonate by competing with acidic (anionic) drugs for renal tubular clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 9. Methylprednisolone decreases the levels of aspirin, citric acid, and sodium bicarbonate by increasing renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 10. Metolazone can increase the levels or effects of aspirin, citric acid, and sodium bicarbonate by competing with acidic (anionic) drugs for renal tubular clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 11. Aspirin, citric acid, and sodium bicarbonate can increase the levels or effects of nabumetone by competing with acidic (anionic) drugs for renal tubular clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 12. Aspirin, citric acid, and sodium bicarbonate can increase the levels or effects of naproxen through acidic (anionic) drug competition for renal tubular clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 13. Aspirin, citric acid, and sodium bicarbonate increase the levels of neomycin (oral) by decreasing renal clearance. This interaction primarily occurs in preterm infants. The clinical significance is unknown. 14. Aspirin, citric acid, and sodium bicarbonate, as well as noni juice, both increase serum potassium levels. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 15. Ofloxacin, when combined with aspirin, citric acid, and sodium bicarbonate, may increase the risk of central nervous system (CNS) stimulation or seizures. This occurs due to the displacement of GABA from its receptors in the brain. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 16. Aspirin, citric acid, and sodium bicarbonate can increase the levels or effects of oxaprozin by competing with acidic (anionic) drugs for renal tubular clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 17. Aspirin, citric acid, and sodium bicarbonate can increase the levels or effects of parecoxib through acidic (anionic) drug competition for renal tubular clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 18. Aspirin, citric acid, and sodium bicarbonate increase the levels of paromomycin by decreasing renal clearance. This interaction primarily occurs in preterm infants. The clinical significance is unknown. 19. Penicillin VK and aspirin, citric acid, and sodium bicarbonate can each increase the levels of the other by decreasing renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 20. Aspirin, citric acid, and sodium bicarbonate, when combined with pentazocine, may increase the toxicity of either drug due to pharmacodynamic synergism. Chronic use may increase the risk of renal papillary necrosis. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown.
